pack.query: After governance changes the minimum gas tip (priority fee / minTip) policy, normal non-validator account transactions get rejected for a while; symptom resolves after a new block with transactions is produced.

citations.note: SetCurrentBlock — the Root != header.Root guard SKIPS the header swap on empty (Root-unchanged) blocks, leaving env.currentBlock pinned to the previous header.
GetAnzeonTipCap — for NON-authorized senders returns env.currentBlock.GasTip(); for authorized (validator) senders returns tx.GasTipCap(). This asymmetry produces the ticket's distinguishing feature.

Header.GasTip() — extracts WBFTExtra.GasTip from the header. Each header's WBFTExtra.GasTip is sourced from the PARENT state in engine.getGasTip, so block N's header carries the OLD policy and block N+1's header carries the NEW policy.
Engine.getGasTip — reads gasTip from PARENT state, then WriteGasTip stamps it into the header WBFTExtra.
WriteGasTip applies the value into WBFTExtra.GasTip.
Backend InheritExtra path — second producer site that re-stamps GasTip on header construction.
LegacyPool.Init — first SetCurrentBlock call on pool startup.
LegacyPool.Pending — SetCurrentBlock(filter.Header) on every miner snapshot; then filters pending using EffectiveGasTipIntCmp(MinTip, anzeonTipEnv).

LegacyPool.reset — fires on ChainHeadEvent for every new head (empty or not); calls anzeonTipEnv.SetCurrentBlock(newHead) at line 1536. The bug is downstream of THIS call: it sees a new head but the inner guard rejects the update.
Reorg loop SetBaseFee on each new head.

Transaction.EffectiveGasTip + anzeonTipCap atomic cache. The cached value on a tx is sourced from env.currentBlock.GasTip() during validation — it's a SECONDARY cache; the root source is env.currentBlock.
ValidateTransaction — tx.GasTipCapIntCmp(opts.MinTip) check uses pool.gasTip (refreshed promptly via worker.SetGasTip).
ValidateTransactionWithState — caches tx.anzeonTipCap via GetAnzeonTipCap(tx). This is where stale env.currentBlock leaks into per-tx cache.
worker.updateGasTipFromContract — refreshes worker.tip and calls TxPool().SetGasTip on every new block. This path IS refreshed promptly even on empty blocks (NOT the source of the bug).
worker.setGasTip → setGasTipUnsafe → TxPool().SetGasTip. Updates pool.gasTip (a SEPARATE atomic from env.currentBlock).

Block import path: bc.gasTipUpdater(state) fires inside go-routine after writeBlockAndSetHead. This refreshes pool.gasTip but NOT env.currentBlock — the latter is updated only via the ChainHeadEvent → pool.reset → SetCurrentBlock path, which is where the broken guard sits.

ckv.note: Governance entry point that updates contract storage gasTip — the trigger for the entire bug scenario.
Reads gasTip from GovValidator storage slot 0x39 — used by both worker.getGasTipFromContract and engine.getGasTip.

callers.note: reset (the ChainHeadEvent-driven call — main production path)
ValidateTransactionWithState — caches anzeonTipCap on the tx.
EffectiveGasTip — fallback when tx cache is nil; used by EffectiveGasTipCmp + EffectiveGasTipIntCmp in priced list and Pending() filter.

concurrency_impact.note: Concurrency analysis: SetCurrentBlock is invoked under pool.mu.Lock() in reset (line 1473)/Pending (line 575)/Init (sequenced before goroutines start) — so writes to env.currentBlock are serialized. GetAnzeonTipCap reads env.currentBlock without the pool lock when called from EffectiveGasTip on a transaction (e.g. inside priceHeap.cmp during Reheap). The fix must NOT introduce a new lock that breaks this layering; updating the header pointer atomically (or under the same pool.mu) suffices.

production_call_sites: core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go:1536 (reset — ChainHeadEvent fires this on EVERY new head)
impacts.downstream_effect: All non-validator-sender effective-tip computations route through env.currentBlock.GasTip(). Stale env.currentBlock corrupts: (1) Pending() filter for the miner, (2) anzeonTipCap cache on freshly-validated txs in ValidateTransactionWithState, (3) priceHeap ordering during Reheap.

domain_classification.reasoning: Touches txpool (legacypool) and consensus-engine produced state (Header.GasTip via WBFTExtra). Concurrent code paths share env.currentBlock between pool reset/Pending writers and EffectiveGasTip readers.

stablenet_invariants_relevant: Invariant #1 (EQUAL POWER) — not violated; tip policy is administrative, not weighting.
Invariant #11 (CONCURRENCY DISCIPLINE) — the fix must not relax txpool/loop discipline; env.currentBlock writes are inside pool.mu.Lock and must stay there.
Invariant #6 (INSTANT FINALITY) — empty-block production after a governance change is normal WBFT operation; the bug is in client-local caching, not consensus.
